pages.notes: Typeset government form with red redaction bars and handwritten classification marks (1.4a); OCR misreads timestamps (1504Z→15042,I; 1515Z→151$2; 1618Z→16182), struggles with overlaid handwritten notations, and mangles redacted content, but captures most narrative and admin sections despite errors.

Military/government form with extensive redactions; OCR captures main structural elements and most field labels correctly, but systematically garbles redaction code characters (§ for ), } for ), missing characters).

Declassified military form with well-structured personnel and equipment fields; OCR captured layout and most text correctly but garbled some redaction code representations (e.g., email field shows noise characters mixed with redaction markers).

Military mission report form with structured timeline sections (Takeoff, Landing, On Station); OCR accurately captured all visible text including redacted fields marked with classification codes; minimal errors.

Declassified military ISR report with structured form data and multiple redaction boxes. OCR captured layout and most content correctly, but struggled with some character recognition (VE«ICLES vs VEHICLES, AS~OCIATED vs ASSOCIATED, ACTVITY vs ACTIVITY, N vs NO) and redaction box handling, where boxes containing '1.4a' sometimes appear as text in the OCR output rather than being properly masked.

Form captures most content correctly, but OCR struggles with black redaction boxes, rendering them as tildes, exclamation marks, and other characters (e.g., 'MDS Type / Asset Type~ 1.4a, 1.4g I' and 'Ha•rison' instead of 'Harrison').

Declassified UAP incident report with heavy redactions; OCR struggled significantly with redaction boxes and had multiple character-level errors: STRAIGHT→IGHT (missing prefix), THEIR→HEIR, SPOTTED→SPOTTE, RTB→RIB, Richard→Ricrard, and Harrison→Har•1sor in the header.
